To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conditional correlation of an individual stock with the market portfolio is a good proxy for the risk premium of the stock, and the conditional correlation of the portfolio with the market is a good proxy to explain the risk premium of a portfolio.

the DCC model is a useful tool to estimate time-varying risk premia, and that the intertemporal CAPM with dynamic conditional correlations provides a useful framework to explain the time-series behavior of expected returns.

1) the DCC model is a good model of conditional covariance; 2) the risk aversion coefficient is positive and significant; and 3) the risk premium induced by conditional covariances with the market and macroeconomic, financial and volatility factors is significant and large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intertemporal capital-asset-pricing model of Merton.
a new approach to testing the intertemporal capital model.
the intertemporal capital-asset pricing model with dynamic correlation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditional covariation between a stock’s (a portfolio’s) return and the return on the market portfolio is a significant determinant of the stock’s (the portfolio’s) expected return.
there is a strong empirical case for time-varying expected returns in the stock market, but it is not yet possible to determine which of several competing explanations is correct.

the intertemporal capital-asset-pricing-model with dynamic conditional correlations, as a generalization of the intertemporal asset pricing model, is a viable model for the joint distribution of asset returns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intertemporal capital model is consistent with the empirical evidence, but it is not the whole story.
the conditional covariance with the stock market is an important determinant of time-variation in asset returns, but that it does not capture all the variation in asset returns.
the conditional covariations between assets and the market are priced in the cross-section.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conditional covariations of assets with the stock market, macroeconomic, and volatility factors are important for explaining the conditional risk premia of assets.
time-variation in a stock’s conditional covariance with the overall market is a source of time-variation in its expected return.

the intertemporal asset pricing model can be extended to allow for time-varying correlations among assets and that the conditional covariance with the portfolio of risky assets can explain time-variation in expected returns.
